name: Oriel Edict-Keeper
campaignHooks: Campaign 02: Trial of the Celestial Heights
loreTies: Oriel stores verdicts about which Realms may intervene when Gates destabilize. Oriel is not a hero; Oriel is a lawful voice inside the hierarchy of radiant survival.
shortBackstory: Oriel Edict-Keeper belongs to The Radiant Hierarchies, the older source behind human myth. Oriel is an edict-keeper formed by angelic hierarchy and living record law. Their glass tablets, bell-metal seals, layered halos, quiet dread, and wing geometry should feel like the origin of later angel-scribe legends.

chapters.title: Before the Gate Spoke
chapters.text: Oriel Edict-Keeper was important before battle records named them. As celestial records officer, Oriel Edict-Keeper learned the hidden machinery beneath The Radiant Hierarchies: who records law, who witnesses oath, who warns the living world, and who profits when warnings are ignored.

chapters.title: Faction Duty
chapters.text: Oriel Edict-Keeper's loyalty is tied to Empyrean culture rather than battlefield glory. Their doctrine is simple and dangerous: Existence survives through order. The story needs them because Titans can win fights and still misunderstand what victory costs.

chapters.title: Story Arc Tie
chapters.text: During Storm-Oath Covenant, Oriel Edict-Keeper becomes a readable witness to campaign consequence. Their first appearance, Campaign 02: Trial of the Celestial Heights, places them where player decisions need interpretation, warning, and memory instead of another controllable unit.

chapters.title: Conflict Wound
chapters.text: The Gate pressures Oriel Edict-Keeper through knowledge. It offers signs that are useful but incomplete, trying to turn witness into accomplice. Their recurring conflict is whether to reveal truth early and risk panic, or wait for proof and risk lives.

chapters.title: Dashboard Role
chapters.text: As a non-playable character, Oriel Edict-Keeper belongs under Characters and Character Backstories. Their profile should be read beside campaign dialogue, codex unlocks, and faction pages so every briefing feels like canon consequence, not tutorial flavor.
